newsitem.title: UK: Solid Boots helps share price recovery.
newsitem.headline: Solid Boots helps share price recovery.

text.p: A solid results performance from Boots The Chemist helped drive a rally in Boots Co Plc's shares on Thursday, after the stock fell back initially to reflect the payment of a special dividend, retail analysts said.

The shares stood five pence lower at 689.5 pence by 1430 GMT, after dropping more than 30 pence earlier in the day. After stripping out the effect of the loss of the special dividend, the shares were actually up on the day.
Analysts' said the results showed that there had been no let up in the core chain Boots The Chemist's relentless progress.
The smaller divisions, apart from A.G. Stanley performed better than expected, also giving the shares a boost.

"There were one or two areas of concern, particularly DIY, but the rest was really positive," said another analyst. Boots Healthcare International's marketing costs were also lower than expected, another said.
Analysts were in the process of adjusting their profit forecasts for the current year, factoring in around a 20 million stg cost for the special dividend.
The range was fairly wide between 560 and 585 million stg, down from around 590 to 595 million stg, but the numbers were still not finalised, analysts said.

Earlier Boots reported a near nine percent increase in pretax profits to 536.2 million stg for the past financial year and said it would pay shareholders a special dividend amounting in total to 400.5 million stg.
